title.narrative: Flash Floods Risk Assessment and Hazard Mapping in Mafraq Wadi (Valley) in Jordan

description.narrative:
The project will focus on strengthening municipal the institutional capacity of Mafraq Municipality to manage climate change, especially related to urban water challenges (i.e. floods) by mainstreaming these aspects into spatial strategies / urban master plans and developing action measures. Thus, through this project, municipal plans will be used as tools to identify and manage climate change risks/vulnerabilities and identify additional adaptation options. The project rationale is to complement the Urban master plan at the Mafraq municipality level conducted by the Adaptation Fund project implemented by UN-Habitat. The project will develop a Vulnerability and Climate Change risk assessment study in Mafraq Wadi and an adaptation plan that includes intervention measures or measures aimed at reducing the flood risk to the targeted area in Mafraq (Mafraq Wadi). The project has two major outcomes activities: Activity Outcome (1): Strengthened Urban resilience and Management of Climate Change Risk and Vulnerability in Mafraq Wadi specifically through understanding the flood risk and defining adaptation priorities and risk reduction measures vulnerability and Climate Change risk assessment in Mafraq Wadi 1.1 “Urban water challenges in Mafraq Wadi are mapped and assessed through Vulnerability and Climate Change risk assessment, which will identify flood hotspots” Preparatory work including consultations with the Mafraq Municipality and local stakeholders and Defining the boundary of the intervention” The project team works on defining the boundary of the area to target in the analysis in a participatory approach with the Municipality of Mafraq to complement the work done within the Adaptation Fund project. 1.2 Drafting the RFP for the consulting firm, The project team will develop TORs /Request for Proposal documents, to complement the Adaptation Fund project work in the same area. 1.3 Conduct the Vulnerability and Climate Change risk assessment in Mafraq Wadi The work required to develop a Flood Risk Assessment and Hazard Mapping Study include: Performing the hydrological and hydraulic modeling and analysis required in the watershed area contributing flow to the entire targeted area, performing a flood risk assessment study for the targeted area, performing hydraulic modeling within the 1000-Year floodplain in the targeted area, and developing floodplain and flood hazard maps of different flood risk events (return intervals) for the targeted area. The vulnerability assessment will include future climate projections including resources affected by climate change risk, such as water, agriculture, soil, infrastructure, land use/land cover, and natural heritage sites among others. Adaptation priorities will be defined according to this assessment. 1.2 Adaptation measures and intervention in Mafraq Wadi are assessed, prioritized, and planned in collaboration with Mafraq Municipality and stakeholders1.4 Draft an adaptation plan to mitigate the risks of flooding in Mafraq Wadi The study should also inform on potential risk mitigation measures (e.g. possible options for infrastructure improvements to mitigate existing and future risks of flooding of Mafraq wadi) which leads eventually to greater urban resilience. Accordingly, the consulting firm will develop an adaptation plan that aims to provide up-to-date evidence-based assessment, improve understanding of the causes for increased flood risks and identify flood hotspot areas in Mafraq wadi that requires immediate intervention. The maps developed in Activity (1.3) should be for the pre and post-intervention conditions of the interventions mentioned in the adaptation plan. 1.5 Develop a concept note for adaptation intervention/project in Mafraq Wadi Based on all the above, the project team will design, in collaboration with the Mafraq Municipality and stakeholders, a concept note for an adaptation intervention/project in the target area.
Activity Outcome (2): Enhanced national and international knowledge exchange on mainstreaming urban water challenges into spatial strategies / urban master plans and implementing evidence-based adaptation measuresInternational /regional knowledge exchange and capacity building
2.1 Municipal capacities in Mafraq are enhanced by mainstreaming water-related climate change adaptation in Urban plans and strategies through a learning-by-doing approach 2.2 International and national knowledge exchange is facilitated through participation in international and regional events, workshops, and conferences, leading to enhanced implementation of the NDCs 2.1 Explore regional and international climate change programs and events to present the project results The project team will prepare a list of climate change-related events, workshops, and conferences that could be used to present the lesson learned and exchange knowledge with other countries and projects on the implementation of the NDCs in the NDCP country’s context. 2.2 Parti
